beats.say: A penny gets you a whole record collection. And the first record costs nothing.
Sign up, get twelve records for a penny.
Pay the regular club price for each future album.
Skip the next shipment and avoid a bill.
If you never say no, a full-price album arrives. Sounds generous.
But it does a job: it forces an automatic purchase.
The penny option is the hook; the silent auto-ship is the trap.
Columbia House peaked at $1.4 billion in 1996, then fell to $17 million by 2014.
When members ignored the deadline, the company collected full-price sales.
A gym offers a $1 trial membership.
If you don't cancel, you're billed $30 each month - the trial disappears.
The $1 trial feels cheap, so you roll into the $30 plan.
A tiny upfront fee can hide a big ongoing bill. Follow for more.
